summary: Map where CLWA engine is universal vs crime-justice-locked; rank engine investments that widen game-creation space

result.summary: I verified the four maps against the live code: INV-14's import boundary is genuinely clean (zero module imports in engine), the AffordanceRequirement crime-vocabulary leak and hardcoded investigator/canSentence branches are real (al.ts:11-49, 332-335), there is NO quantified state anywhere in AgentState (only a dead-end static shop list), CrimeScene is hardcoded in the engine's public API, and MoodModifier is the one existing named-scalar-with-modifiers pattern. The maps are accurate and internally consistent. The engine is ~80-90% genre-extensible at the registry/data plane (events, affordances, scoring, steps, consequences, beliefs, conversation, evidence, lifecycle hooks are all genuinely registry-driven), but it hits a HARD ceiling on quantitative simulation: no resource/inventory/HP/standing/faction state exists, so no second genre can model conserved value, damage, or collective power without faking it in untyped payloads. I ranked 10 options across all four categories. The highest-leverage cluster is: (1) a thin Economy spike to empirically flush blockers, (2) a generic scalar-attribute subsystem generalized from MoodModifier (one primitive backs Economy/Combat/Politics/Survival at once), and (3) the requirement-generalization + capability-registry hardening the spike forces. The single recommendation is to run the spike FIRST, then build the scalar subsystem against the real blockers it exposes — proving generality before abstracting it.
result.visionGap: There is NO quantified state primitive anywhere in the engine. AgentState is entirely symbolic/social (alive, location, mood, status, beliefs, relationships) — confirmed: no balance, no inventory, no HP, no standing, no faction. The only numeric-with-modifiers pattern that exists is MoodModifier. Every second genre the vision names is gated on this same missing shape: Economy needs gold+inventory, Combat needs HP+damage, Politics needs influence+standing, Survival needs need-meters — all are 'a named, clamped, decaying scalar with modifiers and a condition op to read it.' Until the engine has a generic scalar-attribute (and item-transfer) layer, a 2nd genre can only fake quantitative state by stuffing numbers into the untyped event.payload and reimplementing accounting in tick handlers — which violates conservation, has no persistence integrity, and is invisible to CG conditions and affordance scoring. The INV-14 vocabulary leaks (crime-named AffordanceRequirement fields, hardcoded investigator/canSentence branches, CrimeScene in the public API) are real and worth fixing, but they are TYPE-LEVEL smells the registry escape hatches already route around at runtime. The QUANTITATIVE-STATE gap is a hard capability ceiling, not a smell: it is the single thing standing between 'a different crime town' and 'a different game.'

recommendation.title: Ship a minimal Economy spike FIRST, then build the generic scalar-attribute subsystem it exposes
recommendation.rationale: Two of the maps independently converge on the same conclusion: the quantified-resource primitive is the #1 missing capability for a 2nd genre, and a thin 2nd genre reveals more locked assumptions than any amount of analysis. Doing them in this order is the highest-leverage move. The Economy spike (M) is cheap and immediately empirical: it will hit the exact four documented blockers (no resource state, beliefConfidence-only requirement params, hardcoded capability flags, pre-existing ShopItem/TradeIntent/EmotionalPressure-union collisions) and turn the maps' predictions into a concrete, ranked engine-edit list grounded in a running module rather than speculation. Then the scalar-attribute subsystem (L) — built by GENERALIZING the MoodModifier pattern the engine already proves — is the one primitive that simultaneously backs Economy gold, Combat HP, Politics standing, and Survival needs. That single subsystem plus the requirement/capability generalization it forces is what converts the engine from 'crime-content-swappable' to 'genre-extensible,' which is exactly the user's stated goal of widening the game-creation space rather than closing the crime game.
recommendation.tradeoff: The spike's output is intentionally a throwaway/fake economy (numbers in payload, no conservation), which sits in tension with the user's 'build complete systems, no scaffolds' rule — so it must be explicitly framed and time-boxed as a generality PROBE whose deliverable is the blocker list, not a shipped feature, and its fake-state must be torn out and replaced by the real scalar subsystem. The cost is doing the Economy affordances/events twice (once thin against payload, once properly against the new primitive). The alternative — building the scalar subsystem first with no module driving it — risks designing the wrong shape in the abstract and over-engineering transactions/ledgers nobody is exercising yet. Accept the rework as the price of designing the primitive against real, observed module demand.
recommendation.firstConcreteStep: Author a ~80-line minimal Economy module (mirroring social/index.ts, the lean template) registering ONLY: registerEventCategory('economy',['TRADE','FRAUD']) + registerEventLabels + registerEventTypeFlags (FRAUD transferable so beliefs gossip); two AffordanceDefinitions (defraud: high-O/low-A weights, resistTraits honesty:high; trade: cooperative weights) pushed into AFFORDANCE_REGISTRY + registerActionVerbs; one ConsequenceRule FRAUD->REPUTATION_LOSS gated on a trait condition; and a registerStepHandler('attempt_fraud') that today just emits the event. Wire it in server/index.ts alongside registerCrimeJusticeModule. Run it in the existing crime world via the debug API and record EVERY point where you are forced to either edit the engine or stuff state into event.payload. That recorded list — expected to surface the scalar-state gap, the beliefConfidence-only requirement-param limit (al.ts:294), the hardcoded capability branches (al.ts:332-335), and the ShopItem/TradeIntent collision — becomes the precise, prioritized spec for the scalar-attribute subsystem and the requirement/capability hardening that follow.

options.title: Generic scalar-attribute subsystem on AgentState (the universal numeric layer)
options.capability: Add a string-keyed, registry-declared numeric-attribute system on AgentState — a named scalar with base value, clamped range, decaying/timed modifiers, and onChange broadcast. Generalize the EXISTING MoodModifier pattern (agent-types.ts: baseMood + moodModifiers[] + computed effective mood, the only place the engine already does named-decaying-clamped-scalar). Add a RuleCondition op ('attr gt/lt/eq <key>') and a generic AffordanceDefinition scoring-contributor channel so utility and CG rules can read these attributes.
options.unlocks: ONE primitive simultaneously backs health/HP (Combat), gold/wealth balance (Economy), standing/legitimacy/influence (Politics), and need-meters hunger/fatigue (Survival). Affordances can score on situational/resource drivers (smuggle higher when debt high; flee when HP low). CG rules can gate on quantitative world state ('target.gold < 10'). It is the named dependency under Inventory, Needs, Economy, and Combat at once.
options.dependencies: None structurally — MoodModifier already proves the shape. To be fully useful, computeUtility (al.ts:461) needs a pluggable SCORING_CONTRIBUTORS channel and RuleCondition needs the numeric-attr op.
options.risks: Persistence/serialization surface grows (AgentState shape change = save-migration). Risk of re-baking domain semantics into the engine if attribute keys leak crime/economy names — must stay a pure string-keyed registry like events/sources. Scope creep: easy to over-design transactions/ledgers; keep v1 to per-agent scalars + modifiers, defer cross-agent conservation to Inventory.

options.title: Inventory / item-instance / transfer subsystem (Phase 3)
options.capability: Engine-level Item/Container model: item instances with owner+location+state refs, quantities, and an atomic transfer-of-value step primitive (move N of resource X from A to B with conservation). Replaces the dead-end static AgentProfile.shop display list with real transactional state. Provide a generic 'transfer' step handler and a transfer-result the affordance VM can call (today step-handlers theft at step-handlers.ts:216 emits GOODS_STOLEN but mutates NO state because no inventory exists).
options.unlocks: A REAL Economy module (buy/sell/steal that actually moves conserved value), physical evidence (plant/find the knife), crafting, loot, equipment to hold weapons (Combat prerequisite), trade ledgers, smuggling cargo. Turns the ~80-90% reachable economy module into a 100%-reachable one without hacking accounting into event.payload + tick handlers.
options.dependencies: Builds on the scalar-attribute subsystem (quantities) but can ship value-balance first. Needs the generic requirement-param channel (below) so 'cost>=price' gates work as data.
options.risks: Conservation/atomicity is the hard part — partial transfers, failed trades, item duplication bugs. Persistence migration. Must resist re-introducing crime/trade vocabulary in the engine type (item.kind stays a free string). Larger blast radius than scalar attributes alone.

options.title: Faction / group / membership subsystem (Phase 3)
options.capability: Engine Faction/group entity + membership on AgentState + a FACTION_TYPES registry, plus group-scoped relationship/standing (per agent-faction and faction-faction). Today only pairwise RelationshipGraph edges (sentiment/trust) and individual capability booleans exist — there is no collective actor.
options.unlocks: Politics module (alliances, coalitions, decrees, legitimacy), organized crime, families/guilds as actors, territory, faction-scoped belief aggregation. Blocks ANY genre where the unit of action is a collective rather than an individual.
options.dependencies: Strongest with the scalar-attribute subsystem (per-faction standing/influence as scalars). Independent of Inventory.
options.risks: RelationType is a CLOSED union (relationships.ts) with hardcoded DEFAULT_TRUST/grief tables — adding factional relations touches that locked enum. Group-scoped beliefs are a genuinely new modeling axis (Belief is per-agent today) and risk over-design. Lower immediate leverage than scalar+inventory because no in-flight module needs it yet — proving generality matters more first.

options.title: Trauma layer — dynamic personality baselines (Phase 3)
options.capability: A TRAUMA_RULES registry that applies permanent OCEAN+H baseline shifts triggered by events/consequences. Extends the existing Personality Model; personality is static today.
options.unlocks: Character arcs and organic development, Horror, deep Social/Drama, victims hardening into perpetrators. Makes the existing psychology engine evolve over time rather than being fixed at authoring.
options.dependencies: None — extends PM only, no AgentState shape change, no save migration. Cheapest Phase-3 subsystem.
options.risks: Low. Mainly tuning/balance (runaway drift, oscillation). Does not by itself widen the GENRE space (no new resource/spatial/collective primitive) — it deepens existing psychology rather than unlocking a 2nd genre, so it is a deepener not a widener.

options.title: Generalize AffordanceRequirement into a fully registry-resolved keyed map (close the #1 INV-14 leak)
options.capability: Remove the crime-named typed fields from the ENGINE AffordanceRequirement (al.ts:11-49: hasCrimeBelief, isCriminal, isWanted, hasWitnessBelief, notPerpetrator, deductionBelowThreshold, etc.) and the hardcoded inline branches in checkRequirements/checkRequirementsReactive/validatePlayerAction (al.ts:332-335, 365-368, 537-541 — all wired to agent.profile.investigator/canSentence). Make the requirement an open string-keyed map resolved ENTIRELY through REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS, with a GENERIC params bag (today checkRegistryRequirements at al.ts:294 only forwards beliefConfidence). Move noGuardNearby/maxWitnesses post-target checks (al.ts:302-316) and the crime-belief auto-enrichment in findByRole (al.ts:269-280) into the crime module.
options.unlocks: Economy/Politics/Combat requirements (hasCapitalAbove, isOfficeholder, atMarket, hpAbove) become pure DATA with their own numeric params — no engine edit, no field-name abuse. Closes the single biggest INV-14 type-level leak and the documented double-standard (registry exists but bolted ALONGSIDE hardcodes). Makes the 'add Economy with zero engine changes' test pass for requirements.
options.dependencies: Pairs with the capability-registry option (the hardcoded branches read investigator/canSentence flags). The generic params-bag is also needed by Inventory/scalar gates.
options.risks: Refactor touches hot-path requirement evaluation used by both NPC volition AND validatePlayerAction (bilateral parity must be preserved). Must port crime-justice module's checkers without behavior change — needs the existing crime world as a regression oracle. Pure plumbing, no new player-visible value, so it competes for time against shippable features.

options.title: Capability registry — replace hardcoded role booleans with string-keyed capabilities
options.capability: Convert AgentProfile.investigator / detersCrime / canSentence (agent-types.ts:101-106) into a string-keyed capability bag/registry, and extend the existing CG 'has_capability' op (already boolean) into the gating path so the engine never reads a crime-flavored flag directly (al.ts:332-335, 305, volition.ts:169 debug branch).
options.unlocks: New genre roles (canTrade, isFactionLeader, isMerchant, canSmuggle, isSoldier) declared as data, not engine edits. Removes the last hardcoded crime vocabulary from the engine's behavioral control flow. has_capability already exists as a CG op — this just makes it the single source of truth.
options.dependencies: Co-dependent with the AffordanceRequirement generalization (the requirement branches consume these flags). Best done in the same pass.
options.risks: AgentState/profile shape change -> save migration. World-editor and world-loader JSON read these flags today (agent profiles) so the authoring schema must migrate in lockstep. Behavior-preservation against the crime world is the validation bar.

options.title: Abstract CrimeScene -> generic SceneResidue (de-crime the engine public API)
options.capability: Rename/abstract the engine's CrimeScene subsystem (world-types.ts:128 CrimeScene{crimeType,perpetratorId,victimId}; world.ts markCrimeScene/processKill/onMurder/onCrimeScene callbacks; tick-result murder/crimeScene fields) into a genre-neutral 'world-state residue at a location' primitive — examination points, sceneType already a free string. processKill -> generic state-transition event. Move crime vocabulary into the crime module.
options.unlocks: The spatial-residue mechanic (genuinely universal) cleanly serves fraud audit trails, battlefield aftermath, political scandal sites, smuggling spill scenes — WITHOUT inheriting crime-named symbols. Removes a large crime-specific subsystem from the engine layer.
options.dependencies: Touches world.ts core loop + persistence (CrimeSceneJSON) + index.ts exports. Independent of resource work.
options.risks: The LOGIC is already universal (sceneType free string); this is mostly renaming + moving callbacks, so leverage is real but bounded — it widens vocabulary cleanliness, not capability. Public-API rename ripples to modules and the server. Lower urgency than the requirement/capability leaks because a module can already REUSE markCrimeScene today (it just inherits crime-named symbols).

options.title: Thin 2nd module as a generality proof — minimal Economy (TRADE/FRAUD)
options.capability: Author a deliberately minimal Economy module (register-only: registerEventCategory('economy',[TRADE,FRAUD]), affordances buy/sell/defraud with OCEAN+H weights + resistTraits honesty, registerStepHandler for transfer, ConsequenceRule[] FRAUD->REPUTATION_LOSS->REVENGE, belief sources 'ledger_evidence', economy topics, tick-phase debt/price drift). Ship it against the existing world to flush out every place the engine forces an edit.
options.unlocks: A working 2nd genre proving ~80-90% of the registry surface, AND — more importantly — an empirical, ranked list of the exact remaining engine blockers (resource state, requirement params, capability flags, crime-named collisions). A thin genre reveals more locked assumptions than any further analysis.
options.dependencies: Will immediately hit: (1) no quantified resource (forces hacking event.payload accounting), (2) requirement-param channel only forwards beliefConfidence, (3) capability flags hardcoded, (4) pre-existing engine ShopItem/TradeIntent/EmotionalPressure-union to reconcile against. That collision IS the deliverable.
options.risks: Without the scalar/requirement work it produces a 'fake' economy (numbers in payload, no conservation) — acceptable as a probe, dangerous if mistaken for done (violates user's 'build complete systems' rule). Frame explicitly as a generality SPIKE whose output is the blocker list, not a finished module.

options.title: Declarative module manifest — modules as validated data, not 1200 lines of TypeScript
options.capability: A JSON/TS-data manifest format that declares a module's affordances, CG rules, event metadata (flags/categories/labels/mood-shifts), belief sources, requirements, and step-template bindings, validated against registry schemas and loaded by a generic registerModuleFromManifest(). Today authoring a 2nd module = hand-writing TypeScript (crime-justice/index.ts is 1205 lines; social is 80; no manifest exists).
options.unlocks: Closes the 'modules = data, not code' gap (Roadmap Principle 3) that the World Editor only solves for world CONTENT. A designer can define a new GAME (not just a new town) without writing engine-adjacent TypeScript. Foundation for a future module-authoring GUI.
options.dependencies: Should come AFTER the requirement/capability generalization and at least one scalar/resource subsystem — otherwise the manifest schema bakes in today's crime-shaped requirement vocabulary and would need re-cutting. Premature now.
options.risks: High risk of premature abstraction: a manifest designed against today's leaky registries would ossify the crime-shaped requirement fields. Custom logic (target finders, tick handlers, pressure handlers) still needs code, so the manifest covers only the declarative 80% — risk of a leaky abstraction that fragments authoring across data+code. Best deferred until the registry surface is hardened by the second module.

options.title: Generic affected-party / role typing for reactive volition + CG targets
options.capability: Replace the victim-centric assumptions in reactive volition (volition.ts:206-289 requiresRelationToVictim treats event.object as 'victim', sentiment threshold = 'grief') and the death-grief tables (relationships.ts getGriefPenalty) with a generic affected-party typing: beneficiary vs harmed-party vs rival, declared per event/consequence. CG targetMode already has witnesses|affected|all — extend the affected-party semantics to be module-declared.
options.unlocks: Politics/Economy reactions (windfall->beneficiary celebrates; market crash->creditor reacts; alliance->ally rejoices) that don't fit a victim/grief model. Lets non-death, non-harm events drive emotional reactions correctly.
options.dependencies: Cleaner after event metadata is exercised by a 2nd module (the spike reveals which reaction shapes are actually needed). Touches reactive volition hot path.
options.risks: Speculative without a concrete 2nd-genre reaction need driving the shape — risks designing affected-party categories that don't match real module demand. Best informed by the Economy spike rather than designed up front.
